about: Fourteen one-page designs for two fictional products, a compost-pickup homepage and a covered-call income screen, for benchmarking the design critics (design_review and the homepage craft critic). Which pages carry which problems is kept off the box.

review.brief:
Loamwise is a fictional weekly kitchen-compost pickup in a mid-size city. This is its homepage, one page, reviewed on desktop and phone.
Who it is for: people in flats and houses without a garden compost heap who throw away food scraps and would rather have them composted.
Homepage job: show how a weekly pickup works, what it costs and what happens to the scraps, so a household books a first pickup.
Primary action: Book a pickup
Design context: marketing-landing-general
Fictional study: no real pickups, bookings or payments. The page is a static design; links lead nowhere outside this page.

brief.disclosure: Fictional kitchen-compost pickup made for a design study: no real pickups, bookings or payments.
brief.audience: People in flats and houses without a garden compost heap who throw away food scraps and would rather have them composted.
brief.purpose: Show how a weekly pickup works, what it costs and what happens to the scraps, so a household books a first pickup.

concept.name: Kitchen to garden
concept.brief: Warm, practical and a little playful: a soft serif for headings over cream, deep green for every action, flat illustrations drawn for this service and calm, generous space. It should feel like a well-run neighbourhood service.
concept.signature_move: A large serif headline beside an illustration of the kitchen caddy; deep green marks every action.
concept.imagery: Flat inline SVG illustrations in greens and cream, drawn for this service; no photos.

review.brief:
Ledgerline is a fictional covered-call income app. This is its Income screen, reviewed on desktop: the app is used on a large screen.
Who it is for: people who own stocks, sell covered calls on them and check income, open calls and roll decisions a few times a week.
Screen job: show this month's premium income and every open call with its risk, and let the user prepare a roll with every cost visible before confirming it.
Design context: rollcall-trader-workspace
Fictional study: the figures, prices and data source are invented; no accounts, orders or payments are real. The screen is a static snapshot; what happens after pressing a button is outside this review.

brief.disclosure: Fictional covered-call income app made for a design study: the figures, prices and data source are invented; no accounts, orders or payments are real.
brief.audience: People who own stocks, sell covered calls on them and check income, open calls and roll decisions a few times a week, on a large screen.
brief.purpose: Show this month's premium income and every open call with its risk, and let the user prepare a roll with every cost visible before confirming it.

concept.name: Plain ledger
concept.brief: Calm and exact: a plain sans with tabular figures, one deep blue for actions, quiet grey rules and charts that carry the data. It should feel like a careful accountant's ledger.
concept.signature_move: The income chart and the roll order side by side, every cost spelled out before confirming.
concept.imagery: No decorative pictures; the charts are the pictures.
